change.summary: Twitter deliberately suspended the OAuth consumer keys of full-featured third-party clients. Affected apps showed 'Suspended' in the developer portal and every request failed, including authentication. It was per-credential, not platform-wide: a freshly created demo client worked fine.

changelog.note: The first acknowledgement came five days later and claimed enforcement of 'long-standing API rules' — rules whose text only appeared in the Developer Agreement about a week after the suspensions began. No notice was possible from any document.

contract.note: Detectable immediately, but only with the right credentials: the change was scoped to specific client_ids, not to endpoints. A prober using a different app key — or the unauthenticated surface — would have seen healthy responses throughout. Probe with the credential whose behaviour you actually care about.

notes: The exact HTTP status returned is unverified — no contemporary source states it — and devcommunity.x.com blocks automated fetches, so 'no developer-forum post exists' is unverified rather than disproven. Included because the credential-scoped shape is a real design constraint for any prober, not because every detail is nailed down.
